evidence: app/eventyay/base/models/orders.py:94-96 — SecureOrderQuerySet.get_with_secret_check catches Order.DoesNotExist and immediately references the unbound name 'order' (assigned on the failing line), causing an unconditional UnboundLocalError / NameError in the except-branch.

app/eventyay/plugins/banktransfer/views.py:68-71 — state__in tuple for refund filtering contains OrderRefund.REFUND_STATE_CREATED twice instead of a meaningful second state; the deduplicated result filters on only one state when two were clearly intended.

app/eventyay/base/services/orders.py:713-724 — hide_without_voucher branch calls both the helper delete(cp) and then cp.delete() directly; the helper already deletes cp, so the bare cp.delete() is a redundant second call on an already-deleted object.

app/eventyay/base/services/orders.py:191-194 — reactivate_order iterates position.issued_gift_cards.all() but breaks after the first gift card, silently ignoring any remaining gift cards for positions that backed multiple cards.

app/eventyay/eventyay_common/utils.py:64-66 and multiple other locations — 'if cond: return True / return False' pattern that can be replaced with 'return bool(cond)'; present in check_create_permission, and duplicated verbatim in api/auth/api_auth.py, common/permissions.py, presale/checkoutflowstep/confirm_step.py, control/views/product.py, and others.

app/eventyay/cfp/flow.py:153-161 — get_step_url iterates query dict to remove False-valued keys, then immediately re-iterates new_query again to perform the same removal; the second pass is unreachable dead work because the first pass already handled removal via pop.
app/eventyay/presale/utils.py:55 — request.organizer is assigned to itself (request.organizer = request.organizer) in the organizer-domain branch; the line is a no-op.

app/eventyay/features/analytics/graphs/utils.py:77-78 — median_value uses int(round(count / 2)) for the odd-count case, which rounds half-up and can return the element at index count//2 + 1 instead of count//2, giving the wrong median for any list of odd length > 1.

app/eventyay/base/services/cart.py:1355-1377 — _require_locking method has three separate return True paths and one return False; the logic is correct but the structure could be a single expression; not a defect but shows structural noise.
logic_clarity.issues_preventing_higher_score: Three confirmed defects with runtime impact: (1) UnboundLocalError in the timing-safe secret-check path (always crashes on missing order), (2) duplicate state constant in refund filter, (3) double-delete of a cart position. These are not style issues; they affect correctness in payment/order flows.

strengths: Guard clauses are used consistently throughout views and service functions; early-return patterns are readable and intentional.
The checkin logic environment (base/services/checkin.py) is well-structured with named lambdas and clear fallback chains.
Timing-safe comparison via hmac.compare_digest is at least attempted in get_with_secret_check, showing awareness of constant-time requirements.
Boolean-returning properties in most model code use direct boolean expressions rather than if/else ladders.
The cart manager's _require_locking() cleanly separates three independent conditions rather than nesting them.
logic_clarity.issue_character: The codebase has a cluster of copy-paste and inversion errors in payment and order flows — duplicate literal in a state filter, dead branch double-delete, a broken timing-safe fallback that crashes with NameError — alongside a widespread but lower-severity 'if x: return True else: return False' pattern across many modules.
logic_clarity.score_rationale: At the global anchor level, a score around 60 reflects that most of the codebase has correct and readable control flow, but there are several provably wrong branches (NameError in secret-check, double-delete of cart position, silently skipping gift cards after the first) concentrated in high-stakes payment code. The 'return True/False' simplification pattern is cosmetic noise spread widely. The combination of a handful of confirmed runtime defects in critical paths and recurring but less-severe simplification opportunities pushes the score clearly below the 70-75 range for 'mostly correct with isolated issues'.

issues.summary: UnboundLocalError in SecureOrderQuerySet.get_with_secret_check: 'order' referenced before assignment in except-branch
evidence: Line 93: order = self.get(code=code) raises Order.DoesNotExist before 'order' is assigned.
Line 95: except-branch calls order.tagged_secret(tag, dummy_secret) — 'order' is unbound, producing NameError/UnboundLocalError unconditionally when the order does not exist.
issues.suggestion: Replace the except-branch with a dummy call that does not reference 'order': call hmac.compare_digest(dummy_secret[:secret_length].lower(), received_secret[:secret_length].lower()) directly, then re-raise. The 'order' variable must not be referenced in the except-handler where it was never bound.

issues.summary: Identical constant OrderRefund.REFUND_STATE_CREATED used twice in state__in tuple, silently narrowing refund lookup
evidence: Lines 68-71: state__in=(OrderRefund.REFUND_STATE_CREATED, OrderRefund.REFUND_STATE_CREATED) — both elements are identical.

The parallel payment filter on lines 76-79 uses two distinct constants (PAYMENT_STATE_CONFIRMED, PAYMENT_STATE_REFUNDED), indicating the refund filter was intended to have a distinct second state (likely REFUND_STATE_TRANSIT or REFUND_STATE_DONE).
issues.suggestion: Determine which second refund state was intended (REFUND_STATE_TRANSIT is the most plausible match given domain context) and replace the duplicate with it. Add a comment explaining the intended state set.

issues.summary: Double deletion of cart position in hide_without_voucher branch: delete(cp) then cp.delete() on an already-deleted object
evidence: Lines 722-723: delete(cp) calls the local helper which tracks and deletes cp and its addons; then cp.delete() is called unconditionally on the same already-deleted object.
All other branches in _check_positions use either delete(cp) or cp.delete() but not both.
issues.suggestion: Remove the bare cp.delete() call on line 723; the helper delete(cp) already handles deletion including addon cleanup. The extra call is a no-op at best and may raise an IntegrityError or silently fail depending on Django's delete behaviour on already-deleted instances.

issues.summary: reactivate_order breaks after creating a transaction for only the first gift card, silently skipping subsequent gift cards
evidence: Lines 191-194: 'for gc in position.issued_gift_cards.all(): ... break' — the break exits after one iteration unconditionally regardless of how many gift cards exist.
The _cancel_order path (line 447-458) iterates all gift cards without a break, confirming that iterating all is the intended pattern.
issues.suggestion: Remove the break statement. If only one gift card per position is expected by invariant, add an assertion or comment explaining that invariant; do not silently skip subsequent cards.

issues.summary: Widespread 'if cond: return True / return False' pattern across multiple modules instead of 'return bool(cond)'
evidence: eventyay_common/utils.py:64-66: 'if is_create_permission or is_active_staff_session: return True / return False' — the entire body is 'return is_create_permission or is_active_staff_session'.
common/permissions.py:14-17: same pattern in is_admin_mode_active.
At least 6 additional occurrences identified across seed files.
issues.suggestion: Collapse 'if x: return True / return False' to 'return bool(x)' or, where the value is already boolean, 'return x'. Apply consistently to prevent copy-paste of the anti-pattern.

issues.summary: Redundant self-assignment 'request.organizer = request.organizer' in organizer-domain branch of _detect_event
evidence: Line 55: 'request.organizer = request.organizer' — assigns the attribute back to itself, which is a no-op and obscures what the intent was (possibly to set it from a different source such as the resolved URL kwargs).
issues.suggestion: Remove the self-assignment line. If the intent was to re-assign organizer from url.kwargs, replace it with the correct source; if it was a placeholder, delete it entirely.

issues.summary: median_value uses int(round(count / 2)) for odd-length lists, returning the element one position past the true median index
evidence: Lines 77-78: for odd count, the median index should be count // 2 (0-based), but int(round(count / 2)) for any odd count n gives (n+1)/2, which is one past the midpoint. E.g. for count=3: round(1.5)=2, but the median is values[1], not values[2].
issues.suggestion: Replace 'int(round(count / 2))' with 'count // 2' to correctly address the middle element of an odd-length sorted list.

root_causes: Copy-paste errors cluster in payment and order service code: the same structural pattern (delete helper + bare delete, break after first iteration, duplicate constant) recurs across several adjacent functions, suggesting fast copy-and-mutate authorship without test coverage validating edge cases.
The 'if cond: return True else: return False' anti-pattern is too widespread to be accidental; it is likely a team habit or AI-generated code pattern that was not reviewed.
likely_symptoms: bool_simplification_pattern — cosmetic noise, no runtime impact
